passages.text: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
Jeduthun was the musician who led the singing.
This psalm is for worship.

passages.text: In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He gave instructions for Jeduthun.
My soul finds rest in God alone.
God gives me salvation.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־ יְדוּת֗וּן מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃ אַ֣ךְ אֶל־ אֱ֭לֹהִים דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּעָתִֽי׃

passages.text: He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David speaks to the choirmaster.
David says God alone is his rock.
God alone saves David.
God is David’s fortress.
David will not be shaken.
passages.original: אַךְ־ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י לֹא־ אֶמּ֥וֹט רַבָּֽה׃

passages.text: How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you throw him down like a leaning wall or a tottering fence?
passages.sermon:
David speaks in this psalm.
David is the author.
David addresses his enemies.
David asks a question.
He says, “How long will you attack a man?”
He asks, “Will all of you try to bring him down?”
He compares the man to a leaning wall.
He compares the man to a fence about to fall.
David describes the man as weak and unstable.
David says the enemies want to destroy him.
passages.original: עַד־ אָ֤נָה׀ תְּהֽוֹתְת֣וּ עַל אִישׁ֮ תְּרָצְּח֪וּ כֻ֫לְּכֶ֥ם כְּקִ֥יר נָט֑וּי גָּ֝דֵ֗ר הַדְּחוּיָֽה׃

passages.text: They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch; they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.
passages.sermon:
Some people plan to bring down a man from a high position.
They want to remove him.
They love lies.
They speak blessings with their mouths.
But inside, they curse.
Pause and reflect.
My soul, be still before God alone.
My hope comes from God.
passages.original: אַ֤ךְ מִשְּׂאֵת֨וֹ׀ יָעֲצ֣וּ לְהַדִּיחַ֮ יִרְצ֪וּ כָ֫זָ֥ב בְּפִ֥יו יְבָרֵ֑כוּ וּ֝בְקִרְבָּ֗ם יְקַלְלוּ־ סֶֽלָה׃ אַ֣ךְ לֵ֭אלֹהִים דּ֣וֹמִּי נַפְשִׁ֑י כִּי־ מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ תִּקְוָתִֽי׃

passages.text: He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken.
passages.sermon:
God is my rock.
God saves me.
God is my fortress.
I will not be shaken.
passages.original: אַךְ־ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי וִֽישׁוּעָתִ֑י מִ֝שְׂגַּבִּ֗י לֹ֣א אֶמּֽוֹט׃

passages.text: My salvation and my honor rest on God, my strong rock; my refuge is in God.
passages.sermon:
God saves me.
God gives me honor.
God is my strong rock.
God is my refuge.
passages.original: עַל־ אֱ֭לֹהִים יִשְׁעִ֣י וּכְבוֹדִ֑י צוּר־ עֻזִּ֥י מַ֝חְסִ֗י בֵּֽאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah Lowborn men are but a vapor, the exalted but a lie. Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm when he was in the Wilderness of Judah.
God is our refuge.
People, trust in God at all times.
Pour out your hearts before Him.
Lowborn men are only a vapor.
Exalted men are a lie.
If you weigh them on the scales, they rise up and disappear.
Together, all people are only a vapor.
passages.original: בִּטְח֘וּ ב֤וֹ בְכָל־ עֵ֨ת׀ עָ֗ם שִׁפְכֽוּ־ לְפָנָ֥יו לְבַבְכֶ֑ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים מַחֲסֶה־ לָּ֣נוּ סֶֽלָה׃ אַ֤ךְ׀ הֶ֥בֶל בְּנֵֽי־ אָדָם֮ כָּזָ֪ב בְּנֵ֫י אִ֥ישׁ בְּמֹאזְנַ֥יִם לַעֲל֑וֹת הֵ֝֗מָּה מֵהֶ֥בֶל יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: Place no trust in extortion, or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
passages.sermon: Do not trust in extortion.\r\nDo not put hope in stolen goods.\r\nIf your wealth grows, do not set your heart on it.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּבְטְח֣וּ בְעֹשֶׁק֮ וּבְגָזֵ֪ל אַל־ תֶּ֫הְבָּ֥לוּ חַ֤יִל׀ כִּֽי־ יָנ֑וּב אַל־ תָּשִׁ֥יתוּ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God, and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds.
passages.sermon:
God spoke once.
I heard this message twice.
God has all power.
Lord, You have loving devotion.
You repay each person for what he has done.
passages.original: אַחַ֤ת׀ דִּבֶּ֬ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים שְׁתַּֽיִם־ ז֥וּ שָׁמָ֑עְתִּי כִּ֥י עֹ֝֗ז לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ וּלְךָֽ־ אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃
